D013-D009_h001.question:
Lately, everything just feels… heavy. For about five months now, I’ve just been in this deep slump. I find myself tearing up at the smallest things, sometimes for no reason at all. It’s hard to even get around the enclosures at work; I feel like I'm moving through molasses. And the thoughts… they just go around and around. I keep replaying every stupid thing I’ve ever said or done, telling myself what a failure I am, how I’m not good enough for my wife. Sometimes, all of a sudden, I’ll get these terrifying urges, like wanting to step right in front of a car, or imagining what it’d be like to jump from a high ledge. I’d never act on them, but they just pop into my head and scare me. It’s gotten so bad I can barely manage my duties at the zoo, and home life is strained.

The thing is, it’s not always like this. There have been times, not quite like feeling on top of the world, but definitely a huge contrast to this. I remember a few years ago, I had a period where I was incredibly productive, barely needed sleep for days, and felt absolutely buzzing with energy. I'd initiate all sorts of projects at the zoo, talking a mile a minute, feeling unusually confident. My wife even commented on how different I was, saying I was
"on fire." It lasted for about a week. It wasn't full-blown mania, I was still functional, but it was certainly a distinct change from my usual self, and a far cry from how I feel now.
D013-D009_h001.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D013-D009_h002.question:
It's been about five months now that I’ve felt this dark cloud hanging over me. I often find myself just staring at my screen, hands restless, rubbing my temples or tapping my fingers constantly, unable to focus on any new code. It's like a heavy weight, and the tears just come out of nowhere, often for no real reason other than just feeling completely overwhelmed. I keep thinking about how much I’ve messed up, replaying every minor mistake at work or with friends, feeling like I deserve everything bad that happens. Honestly, sometimes I just wish I could disappear, or that I just wouldn't wake up in the morning. This isn't just a bad mood; it’s really affecting my work and I’ve been calling in sick a lot more than I should.

The thing is, it's not always like this. There are times, not long ago maybe six months or so, where I feel completely different. I get this surge of energy, like I could code for days without sleep, my mind racing with so many brilliant ideas for new apps. I feel on top of the world, super productive and incredibly outgoing, even if it sometimes means spending a bit too much money or talking a mile a minute. Those periods only last a few days, maybe a week, and then I crash back down into all of this. During those times even my friends comment on how different I get.
D013-D009_h002.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D013-D009_h003.question: I’m here because honestly, I just feel… empty. Like there’s nothing inside me. It's been going on for about five months now. I used to love my job, figuring out how people interact with technology, but lately, I can barely focus. I find myself constantly fidgeting, picking at my cuticles until they bleed, or just pacing around the apartment when I should be working. My husband notices; he tries to help, but I just feel so worthless, like I’m a burden to him and everyone else. Sometimes, I just wish I wouldn't wake up. It’s not that I would do anything, I just… I wouldn’t mind if it all just stopped. This isn't how I usually am. A while ago, about a year back, I had this period where I was on top of the world. I was so productive, barely sleeping, just churning out amazing work, feeling like I could conquer anything. It didn’t last long, maybe a week or so, and I felt great, but in hindsight, it stands out so much compared to how heavy I feel now.
D013-D009_h003.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D013-D009_h004.question:
Lately, it feels like a heavy blanket has been draped over everything. For the past five months, I’ve just felt this profound sadness that I can’t shake. Even getting out of bed to go to the restaurant feels like an immense effort. My movements have slowed down so much, my husband even points out how I drag my feet or take forever to pick up ingredients. I just feel so worthless, like I'm a burden to everyone, a failure at work and at home. There have been days where I just think, "I wish I could just disappear," or "What's the point of going on?" The suicidal thoughts come and go, but I'd never act on them.

It's strange because this isn't my usual self. I remember a few years ago, there was a period, lasted about a week, when I was completely different—full of energy, barely sleeping, finishing projects at the restaurant in record time, my mind racing with ideas. I was so productive and felt on top of the world. Everyone around me noticed the change; my husband even commented on how unusually talkative and driven I was, but I didn't see it as a problem at the time. I never felt so good! But then it faded, and I went back to normal, until now. The current slump is just… crushing.
D013-D009_h004.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D013-D009_h005.question:
Lately, it’s just been this incredibly heavy sadness that won't lift, for about five months now. It's like a dark cloud has settled over everything, and I just can't shake it. I find myself constantly fidgeting, wringing my hands, or pacing around the apartment, unable to sit still, especially after a rough call at work. I feel so guilty all the time, even over tiny things, like if a call doesn't go perfectly, I torture myself about it for days, feeling like I’ve messed everything up. Honestly, sometimes I just wish I could disappear; I have these thoughts of "I want to die" or "I want to kill myself," not with a plan or anything, just this overwhelming desire for it all to stop. It's gotten so bad that it’s hard to focus at work.

But then, it’s weird because before all this started, there were times, usually for a few days, when I’d feel incredibly energized, almost buzzing. I'd need way less sleep, maybe only a couple of hours, and I’d still be full of ideas, talking a mile a minute, bouncing from one project to another, feeling like I could conquer anything. It wasn't full-blown mania, I was still functional, even productive, but it was definitely noticeable to people around me, a stark contrast to how I am now.
D013-D009_h005.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D013-D009_h006.question:
Lately, it’s like I’m moving through treacle. Everything feels heavy, dull, like I'm watching my life unfold through frosted glass. Even my husband, bless his heart, can’t seem to pull me out of it. I'm sleeping so much, ten, twelve hours a night, and still, I wake up exhausted, wanting to just go back to bed. Making even the simplest decisions, like what to make for dinner or what to wear, feels impossible. My mind just churns and I get nowhere. It’s been like this for about two months now, and it’s really getting in the way of everything. Most concerning, there are these terrifying impulses, just fleeting urges to step in front of a bus or jump off my balcony, even though I don't truly want to die. It's so distressing.

But it’s not always like this. Sometimes, I’ll have these periods, usually lasting a few days, where I feel absolutely fantastic, full of energy, needing very little sleep. I’ll start cleaning the whole house at 3 AM or plan elaborate lessons for my old students, even though I'm retired. I’ll talk a mile a minute and feel incredibly creative and productive. My husband usually notices too, saying I'm "on one" again. It throws me off balance, but in a way, it’s a relief from this current gloom. I've had these intense ups and downs for years, and while the "up" phases can be disruptive, they've never landed me in serious trouble or the hospital.
D013-D009_h006.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D013-D009_h007.question: It’s been a rough couple of months, doctor. I just feel this crushing sadness that never really lifts. It’s not just a bad mood; it's like a heavy blanket over everything. I can barely focus on my cases anymore, even during court. My mind just drifts, and I lose my train of thought mid-sentence. Sleep is a joke – I wake up constantly throughout the night and just lie there, replaying all my mistakes. Sometimes, I even think about how much easier it would be if I just wasn't here, contemplating specific ways I could make that happen. But the thing is, this isn't entirely new. Before this deep low hit, about six months ago, I had a period where I was incredibly productive, barely slept, and felt on top of the world for several days, almost like I could conquer anything. My ex-wife even commented on it, saying I was acting erratically. I remember feeling so energized and creative, handling multiple complex cases with ease, which now feels like a distant memory.
D013-D009_h007.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D013-D009_h008.question:
"I know I haven't been myself lately, doctor. It's been a good two months now where this sadness just… hangs over me. It's not just a bad day; it's constant, like a dark cloud. I'm 70, a widow, a retired nurse, and I used to be so active, but now I just want to stay in bed. The nights aren't much better; I'm plagued by these distressing nightmares that leave me exhausted. My thoughts feel so foggy, dazed, like I can’t quite grasp anything clearly. Sometimes, the idea of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' just pops into my head, though I’d never act on it. It’s just this desperate wish for the pain to stop.

What's really confusing is that sometimes, maybe a few times a year, I'll have these periods where I'm just… buzzing. Suddenly I’ll have all this energy, feel incredibly sharp, need hardly any sleep, and just get so much done. I remember one time, I reorganized my entire house in a weekend, felt on top of the world, like I could do anything. My family has even commented on these 'up' spells over the years. It only lasts a few days, maybe a week, and then I crash back down like this. This extreme low is what’s stopping me from living my life."
D013-D009_h008.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D013-D009_h009.question: "Everything just feels… heavy, doctor. It’s been about two months now. I wake up before dawn almost every day, my mind racing, and then I just lie there, staring at the ceiling, feeling this overwhelming sadness I can't shake. It's like a fog has settled in my brain. I can’t remember where I put anything anymore, which is a real problem with my cleaning work – I feel like I’m losing my touch, and I’m so worried about little things, like if I’ve locked the door.  It got so bad a few weeks ago, I actually considered just… ending it all. I counted out my pain pills and even started writing a note to my kids, but I just couldn't go through with it.  The funny thing is, a few times in the past, maybe a year or so ago, I remember having these bursts of energy where I’d clean the whole house top to bottom in a day, barely sleeping, feeling on top of the world. D013-D009_h009.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D013-D009_h010.question:
"Lately, it's just been a struggle to get out of bed. I could easily sleep for 10, 12 hours a day, and even then, I feel exhausted. My wife Rachael says I've been crying at the drop of a hat for about two months now, and she's right. I can't even tell you how many times I've found myself just staring at my hands, feeling the tears well up over nothing. Sometimes, when I’m up on a roof, out of nowhere, I get this terrifying urge to just step off, or when I'm driving, to swerve into oncoming traffic, even though I know I never would. It's really upsetting.

I barely slept – two or three hours felt like enough – and I was talking a mile a minute, bouncing from one project to another, feeling on top of the world. Rachael said I was acting totally out of character, a bit too impulsive and irritable, but I felt amazing. That’s how I knew this current slump wasn’t just a regular bad mood; I've had these incredible highs too."
D013-D009_h010.options:

    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D013-D009_h011.question:
"Lately, I've just felt… heavy. This sadness has clung to me for the past ten months, a constant shadow that no matter what I do, it won't lift. Even getting out of bed feels like a monumental effort; this chronic fatigue is something I’ve never experienced before, and sleep doesn't touch it. My work, my cases, things I used to live for… I just don't care anymore. Solving a tough case, getting a commendation, it all feels meaningless. My wife says I’ve changed, that I’m not the man she married. I can't even focus on a conversation, let alone dive into a detailed report or follow a lead like I used to. It's affecting everything, spilling into every corner of my life.

But it’s not always like this. There have been times, fleeting moments, where it’s like a switch flips. For a few days, I’ll be incredibly energetic, needing hardly any sleep, my mind racing with ideas, feeling on top of the world. I remember one time, not too long ago, I suddenly decided to completely overhaul our garage, working non-stop for two nights straight with an intensity that surprised even me. My wife thought it was great at first, but then she got worried because I was barely sleeping and my thoughts were jumping all over the place. Those periods, I feel fantastic, like I can do anything; I’m more talkative, quicker, almost a different person. But then it always crashes back down to this heavy despair."
D013-D009_h011.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D013-D009_h012.question:

D013-D009_h013.question:

D013-D009_h014.question:

D013-D009_h016.question:
"Well, doctor, it's been a long time now – almost a year and a half, I reckon – that I've just felt… hollow. My wife, bless her soul, passed over three years ago, and while I miss her terribly, this is different. I used to enjoy my weekly card game with the lads, but now I just can't bring myself to go. It feels like too much effort, and I’d just be a burden anyway. Even after a full night's sleep, I wake up feeling just as tired as when I lay down. Sometimes, I just can't sit still, find myself pacing the house or rubbing my hands raw. I keep thinking about things I could've done differently, little mistakes from years ago, and I feel this crushing guilt, like I deserve all this misery.

But you know, it's not always been like this. There was a period, maybe a couple of years back, after Martha died, where I just felt… full of life. I barely slept, felt like I had endless energy, and started planning all these new projects for the garden, even though my knees aren't what they used to be. I was spending a bit more too, just felt like I needed to buy things. My daughter said I was 'acting a bit out of character' then, like I was moving too fast. It only lasted a few days, maybe a week, and then I crashed back down into this. Now, I can barely manage to get dressed most mornings."
D013-D009_h016.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D013-D009_h017.question: I'm just… exhausted, doctor. It’s been about a year and seven months of this heavy fog. Nothing brings me joy anymore. The old ladies at the hospice, my garden – things that used to make me light up, now they just feel… flat. I barely sleep through the night; I’m constantly waking up, staring at the ceiling.     B. Major Depressive Disorder

D013-D009_h018.question:

Flying, which used to be my life's passion, feels like a chore. Even spending time with my wife, it’s not the same. I go to bed, I sleep, but I wake up feeling like I haven't slept a wink, still drained. Everything feels so slow, like my body is moving through molasses, even just getting up to walk to the cockpit. I feel so worthless, like I'm failing at everything – my job, my marriage, just existing. It's gotten so bad that I'm on extended leave; I just can't function at work.

I'll get this surge of energy, practically buzzing, and I can go with very little sleep, feeling totally refreshed. My thoughts race, ideas come to me quickly, and I get so much done, almost too much. My wife even mentioned how I was talking a mile a minute and seemed unusually upbeat a few times last year. It’s never lasted more than a few days, maybe a week, and then I crash right back into this deep hole I’m in now. It's like I have these brief periods where I'm on top of the world, but it eventually fades.
D013-D009_h018.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D013-D009_h019.question:
"Honestly, doc, I’m just… tired. For the past year and seven months, it’s been a real struggle just to get through the day. I used to love catching up with my buddies between fares, but now I just drive home and keep to myself. Even my kids, I barely see them, which just makes me feel like a completely worthless dad. I’m sleeping like twelve hours a night and still feeling exhausted, even dozing off in the back of the cab sometimes when I'm waiting for a fare. I try to stay busy, you know, but sometimes I just find myself pacing around the apartment, rubbing my hands raw, or picking at my cuticles without even realizing it. It's like I can't settle.

I know what you might be thinking, just a guy feeling down, but there’s more to it. There have been times, not recently, but in the past, where I’ve felt completely different. I’d be buzzing with energy, need hardly any sleep for days, feel like I could conquer the world, and make some pretty impulsive decisions, like that time I bought a whole new, expensive sound system for my apartment on a whim. Those periods, when I’m on top of the world and feel like a million bucks, they usually only last a few days, maybe a week, before crashing right back down. It's not usually a wild, out-of-control kind of thing, but it’s definitely a shift. It’s those highs and then these crushing lows that are really messing with my life."
D013-D009_h019.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D013-D009_h020.question:
It’s been, I guess, a year and seven months now, maybe a bit more, that things have felt… heavy. Every morning it’s the same thing: I wake up from some nightmare, usually about being trapped or just really awful, upsetting stuff, and I just don't want to get out of bed. Even when something good happens at work, like a customer complimenting me or the manager saying I did a good job, it just doesn’t stick. It feels meaningless, like, so what? I’m just a gas station attendant. I feel pretty useless, like I’m not good for anything important.

When people ask me a question, it’s like my brain just takes its time spinning up. I know what I want to say eventually, but the words come out so slow, and there’s always a pause. But then, there are these other times. Not right now, but they happen. I’ll feel totally wired, energetic, like I can do anything for a few days. I’ll talk a mile a minute, jump from one crazy idea to another, and need barely any sleep. It felt amazing, like being on top of the world. But it never lasts, and then it’s back to this. It’s like I have these two completely different selves, and it's exhausting.
D013-D009_h020.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D013-D009_h021.question:
Lately, it feels like I'm just going through the motions. Everything is dull, muted; I can't quite access my feelings, good or bad. I spend most of my days in bed, easily sleeping 12 to 14 hours, but still waking up feeling exhausted. My mind is a fog. I forget simple things, like where I put my phone just minutes ago, or what I was about to say. It's been like this for over a year now, about 15 months, and it's really messed up my job search—I can barely focus enough to fill out applications.

What really scares me are the thoughts. I've been thinking about dying, and it’s not just a passing thought. I've actually planned out how I’d do it, where, and when. But it’s weird, because every now and then, I have these periods lasting a few days where I’m wired, full of energy, needing almost no sleep, coming up with all these grand ideas, though nothing ever comes of them. I even recall a time last year, things got particularly intense for about a week – I was buzzing with energy, incredibly productive, way more talkative than usual, almost like an altered state, but it just faded and I crashed right back into this sadness.
D013-D009_h021.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D013-D009_h022.question:

It's more than just feeling sad; it’s like a heavy cloud constantly hangs over me. Even when I get a full night's sleep, I wake up feeling just as tired, if not more so. My memory’s shot; I’m constantly losing my keys or forgetting what I was just about to do, which isn't great for my line of work. Lately, I've had these terrifying urges to do something impulsive, like just step right into traffic, even though I'd never actually do it. It’s scary to feel that out of control.

People have even commented on how fast I’m talking, or how I seem to jump from one idea to the next. These episodes don't last as long as the lows, but they're definitely noticeable and they've happened more than once before this long depressive slump started. It’s like I have these two completely different selves, and the low one has really been in charge lately, making it hard to even get through my days.
D013-D009_h022.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D013-D009_h023.question:
Honestly, I'm just so tired. It’s been over a year now, about fifteen months I think, and it feels like I’m constantly on the verge of tears. Everything makes me cry. Getting to sleep is a battle; I just lie there for hours, my mind racing. Even picking out what to wear for rehearsal feels impossible, let alone deciding what to eat. Sometimes, I’ll be waiting for the subway and this sudden urge, like a jolt, hits me to just… step in front of it. I don’t want to die, but the thought just flashes there. This whole thing has made it really hard to even get on stage.

It’s confusing, though, because sometimes, it's like a switch flips. For a few days, I’ll have all this energy, buzzing with ideas for new choreography, barely sleeping an hour or two. I’ll feel amazing, like I could conquer the world, and I’ll get so much done. It freaks my friends out sometimes, how fast I talk. But then it crashes, and I’m back to this… this heavy despair again. It’s like these high-energy periods are followed by these deep lows.
D013-D009_h023.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D013-D009_h024.question:
"It's been over a year now, about fifteen months, that I've felt... empty. It’s strange, like my emotions are just muted, like I’m watching life through a pane of thick, frosted glass. I sleep, sometimes for what feels like forever, but I wake up just as tired, never refreshed. My mind feels so foggy, like trying to think through a haze – it’s made studying for my Master’s nearly impossible, and my grades have really slipped. Sometimes, I just wish I wouldn't wake up, not that I’d ever do anything, I just want the quiet.

But then there are these other times. A few months ago, for about a week, I was practically buzzing. I barely slept, maybe two or three hours a night, but I felt fantastic, so productive, like I could conquer anything. I reorganized my entire apartment, wrote three chapters of my thesis, and was just overflowing with ideas. I went out every night, talking a mile a minute, feeling like the life of the party. It wasn't like this all the time, just these distinct periods, but I distinctly remember a few times in the past when I’ve felt that same surge of energy and boundless confidence, lasting for a handful of days."
D013-D009_h024.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D013-D009_h025.question:
"I'm here because… well, I just feel empty. For over a year now, about 15 months, it's been this persistent void inside me. I sleep, sometimes for ages, but I never feel rested, always tired. My concentration is shot. As a lawyer, that's a real problem – I can barely focus on a brief, let alone follow a complex argument. My ex-wife even noticed how much I've pulled back. Sometimes I think about just ending it all, and I've even mapped out how I'd do it, where and when. It feels like such a relief to even consider.

But then there are other times, scattered throughout these dark periods, when it’s completely different. Not for very long, usually just a few days, but I suddenly have boundless energy, feel on top of the world. My thoughts بتكون racing, I feel like I don't need sleep at all and I'm incredibly productive. I've had these surges before, years ago too. It's like I swing between this absolute emptiness and feeling intensely "up," almost invincible, even making some impulsive decisions back then."
D013-D009_h025.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
